analysis.title: The Gold Standard: Market Review – November 13
key_insights: Week to Nov 13: S&P 500 +2.5% to 7,562 and VIX -6.3 to 19.3, while gold fell 4.6% to $3,884/oz and silver fell 6.1% to $48.74/oz. Precious metals sold off while US equities rose.

The 10Y Treasury yield rose 28bps to 5.14%. RBC attributes this to a 27bps rise in the 10Y real yield (TIPS) to 2.89%, with 10Y inflation expectations up 1bp to 2.25%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 2bps to 0.29%. 10Y yield sits against a 52-week range of 3.94% to 5.30%.

The dollar index rose 1.1% to 103.4, which is the top of its 52-week range (96.2 to 103.4). Weekly gold correlations in the report are -0.31 with 10Y TIPS and -0.48 with DXY over 3 months, and -0.39 with each over 1 year. Larger FX moves were the South African rand (-2.4% vs USD) and the Swiss franc (-2.2%).

Gold at $3,884 is close to the bottom of its 52-week range ($3,875 to $5,417), and silver at $48.74 sits exactly at its 52-week low (range $48.74 to $116.70). Gold is -10.1% YTD and -10.7% over 3 months. Silver is -32.0% YTD and -24.4% over 3 months.
Physical gold ETFs saw outflows of 217koz in the week and global holdings stand at 101moz. Physical silver ETFs recorded flat flows (0moz) with holdings of 815moz and -21moz quarter-to-date.
CFTC net long gold positions fell 9k to 171k contracts (data as of Nov 3), down 48.1k YTD. Net long silver positions rose 1k to 18k contracts.
Gold equities underperformed gold: GDX -6.8% to $81.64, GDXJ -8.1%, XAU index -6.6%, HUI -7.6%. Gold equity ETFs saw outflows of $511m and silver equity ETFs outflows of $18m.

Worst weekly movers relative to the index were Novagold (-12.0%), DPM Metals (-11.4%), Eldorado Gold (-11.2%), Hecla Mining (-11.1%) and Osisko Gold Group (-10.8%). Senior producers averaged -7%, intermediates -8%, and growth producers -11% on an equal-weighted basis.

US short interest (last reported Oct 30) rose notably at Hycroft Mining (26.0% of float, +2.3pts), Novagold (11.2% combined, +1.3pts), Fortuna Mining, i-80 Gold, Eldorado Gold (7.4% combined, +1.2pts) and Triple Flag. It fell at Perpetua Resources (-1.4pts combined). GDX short interest is 8.8% of float (-0.9pts) and GLD 5.2% (+0.3pts).

Other commodities weakened: copper -2.4% to $6.18/lb (Comex futures table shows $6.09), WTI -2.5% to $88.56/bbl, Brent -2.2% to $96.12, platinum -3.0%, palladium -2.0%. Bitcoin fell 9.7% to $68.3k, -22.0% YTD.

Credit and rates context: USD high yield OAS tightened 24bps on the week to 312bps and investment grade OAS tightened 5bps to 86bps in the performance table. The 2Y yield rose 33bps to 4.84% and the 30Y rose 20bps to 5.47%.

Sector performance in the S&P 500 was broad: energy +5.1%, industrials +3.7%, telecom +3.5%, while materials lagged at +0.3%. Nikkei +6.5% and Euro Stoxx 50 +3.5% led global indices, and Hang Seng fell 3.4%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Latest US CPI year-over-year reading shown in the report's global CPI chart, alongside PPI at 6.5% and import prices at 8.1% year-over-year. No commentary is attached.

RBC cites the rise in real yields as the main driver of the 28bps weekly rise in the 10Y nominal yield to 5.14%, a headwind for non-yielding gold.

crypto_views: Bitcoin fell 9.7% on the week to $68.3k (XBTUSD $68,287), -16.4% over 1 month, -22.0% YTD and -30.8% over 1 year. The report offers no commentary beyond the price data.
risk_factors: Rising US real yields (10Y TIPS 2.89%, +27bps in a week) and a stronger dollar (DXY 103.4, at the top of its 52-week range) are the pressures coinciding with the gold and silver decline.
Gold and silver are at or near 52-week lows ($3,884 vs $3,875 low and $48.74 vs $48.74 low), and gold miners fell more than bullion on the week.

vol_and_positioning: VIX fell 6.3 points to 19.3 while the CBOE Gold ETF Volatility Index (GVZ) was 25.4, -0.6% on the week.
CFTC net long non-commercial gold positions of 171.4k contracts are down 28.3k over 1 month and 43.5k over 3 months. Silver net long is 18k contracts.
GDX short interest is 8.8% of float and GDXJ 6.0%. GLD short interest was 4.5% at Oct 30 per the chart, and 5.2% in the short interest table. SLV is 4.8% per the chart and 5.2% in the table.
Gold equity ETF outflows were $511m on the week and YTD GDX and GDXJ flows are -$595m. Silver equity ETF outflows were $18m.
